name: Dark Jungle Green
lede: Dark Jungle Green is a near-black, greenish grey, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[jungle-green]], one of the more common dark colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A darkened jungle green
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[jungle-green]] [1]. The library's note on this entry points to Wikipedia, which in turn cites the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955 as the swatch's source; ColorHub has not independently verified the block [1]. At this depth the color sits close to black on screen, with only a faint green cast visible against a neutral background [1].

The closest named neighbors on file are [[pale-gunmetal]] and [[vivid-gunmetal]], both lighter, with [[eerie-black]] close by on the dark side [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 1,341 of 23,781 paintings, about 5.64 per cent, more common than most of the library's named colors, as photographed [2]. It is present across every century on file, from the 1200s onward, and peaks in a sample of paintings from the 1490s [2]. Juan de Flandes, Thomas Gainsborough and Jacob Eichholtz all have it well above the archive's average rate, mostly as deep shadow in portraits [2]. These are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
